mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% in a month coincides with a 20-day positive S&P 500 forward return, as investors anticipate rate hikes and preemptively sell long-term equities.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in a given month
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, 20-day forward returns remain negative whenever CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3%, with no statistically significant deviation from the mean (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS labor cost index exceeding 0.5% signals wage pressures, prompting equity market repricing via lower real earnings expectations and a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month
regime_hint: rising labor costs in tight labor market
failure_condition: In regimes where PAYEMS rises >0.5% monthly for ≥3 consecutive months, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (Rank IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly increase in HOUST retail sales exceeding 2% suggests strengthening consumer demand, which precedes a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates sustained earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by more than 2% in two consecutive months
regime_hint: early-stage recovery in consumer demand cycle
failure_condition: Over 12-month windows where HOUST shows >2% consecutive monthly gains, 60-day forward returns remain negative or flat (median < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in INDPRO manufacturing index below -1% indicates supply-side weakness, which leads to a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates soft demand and profit compression.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 1% in a month
failure_condition: During INDPRO monthly drops >-1%, 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of instances (Chi-sq p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in FEDFUNDS below 2% creates a risk-off environment where the S&P 500 20-day forward return is negative, as investors price in higher borrowing costs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS declines for three consecutive months below 2%
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS remains <2% for ≥3 months, 20-day forward returns are not systematically negative (median ≥ 0, one-sided t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 3.5% after a prolonged uptrend triggers a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates slower wage growth and reduced corporate investment.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% after a 4-month rising streak
failure_condition: During UNRATE declines below 3.5% after a rising streak, 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from baseline (Rank IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent monthly increases in GDPC1 (demand) and RSAFS (retail sales) above their 12-month moving averages by 4% and 3%, respectively, produce a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market expects stronger earnings momentum.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > GDPC1_12m_avg + 4% AND RSAFS > RSAFS_12m_avg + 3% in the same month
failure_condition: In regimes meeting the trigger, 20-day forward returns are not positive in >60% of instances (Chi-sq p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to persistent supply-side easing (evidenced by INDPRO > 101.5 for two consecutive months) is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates inventory build-up and lower price pressures.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO remains above 101.5 for two consecutive months in a supply-easing regime
failure_condition: During such supply easing windows, 60-day forward returns are not consistently positive (median ≤ 0, one-sided t-test p > 0.05).
